title: Meeting Rooms
prompt: Given an array of meeting time intervals `intervals` where `intervals[i] = [start, end]`, determine whether a single person could attend all of the meetings (i.e. whether no two meetings overlap). Return `True` if all meetings can be attended, or `False` if any two meetings overlap.

examples.explanation: The two meetings do not overlap.

hints: If the meetings were sorted by start time, would overlaps be easier to spot?
After sorting by start time, an overlap can only happen between a meeting and the one right before it.
Walk the sorted list and check: does the current meeting's start come before the previous meeting's end? If so, they conflict.

solution.approach: Sort the intervals by start time. Then scan through consecutive pairs: if the current interval's start is strictly less than the previous interval's end, there's an overlap and the person can't attend all meetings. If no such pair exists after sorting, all meetings are attendable.
